//: Copy this file to  C:\Swarnakshi\app\appsettings.Production.json  on the server and edit it.
It is the one place the server's settings live. Deploy.ps1 reads it, never overwrites it, and
preserves it across every upgrade - so an edit here survives the next deployment.
After changing anything in this file:   Restart-Service Swarnakshi
This template is committed. The copy on the server holds real passwords and is git-ignored;
do not commit it, and do not copy it back into the repository.
Server        - machine and instance. '.' or 'localhost' is this machine.
Examples:  .\SQLEXPRESS   |   localhost   |   SQLBOX01\SQLEXPRESS   |   10.0.0.5,1433
Database      - the database name.
User ID       - SQL login. For Windows authentication instead, drop User ID and Password
and add  Trusted_Connection=True;  (the service runs as LocalSystem, so the
login to grant is then  DOMAIN\MACHINENAME$ ).
Password      - the SQL login's password. Change it here and restart the service.
TrustServerCertificate - True unless the SQL Server has a certificate this machine trusts.
Key signs every access and refresh token. It must be at least 32 characters, and the app
refuses to start without it. Generate one once and then LEAVE IT ALONE - changing it signs
every user out. To generate one:
powershell -c "$b=New-Object byte[] 48;(New-Object Security.Cryptography.RNGCryptoServiceProvider).GetBytes($b);[Convert]::ToBase64String($b)"

//Urls: The address and port the service listens on. 0.0.0.0 accepts connections from other machines; use localhost to keep it to this one. Remember to open the port in the firewall.
